gacs.t6p: Besides the BACS there is a separate inspection obligation for heating and air-conditioning systems, with its own threshold. That is a different obligation from the BACS. We keep the two apart for you.
gacs.t6h: Please note: inspection is something else
gacs.t5p: Automatic lighting control also drops to the 70 kW threshold, with the same requirement for zones and presence detection.
meta.gebouwautomatisering-gacs.html.desc: Since 1 January 2026, non-residential buildings with a heating or air-conditioning system above 290 kW must have a BACS. What this means for your hotel and where the Lemnion EMS fits in.
gacs.sub: Since 1 January 2026, non-residential buildings with a heating or air-conditioning system above 290 kW must have a building automation and control system. Since 29 May 2026, additional and more sharply defined requirements apply on top of that. For hotels this is not a formality, because the requirements touch exactly the installations that shape your guest comfort. We map out what your building needs.
gacs.wat-h2: The system that makes your installations work together
gacs.wat-p: A building automation and control system (BACS) reads and controls the climate installations in your building. It is not a product you buy in a box, but a coherent whole of control, measurement and analysis on top of your existing installations. It has to measure energy continuously, analyse where efficiency is being lost, inform you as the owner how to improve, and be able to work with equipment from different manufacturers. In practice this is exactly where most buildings fall short: there is a controller, but no layer that measures, analyses and reports.
gacs.wie-h2: The threshold and who is addressed
gacs.g1p: The obligation applies to a heating system above 290 kW or an air-conditioning system above 290 kW. The two are assessed separately, not added together.
gacs.g2p: The obligation rests with the building owner, even if you let it out. If you own the building and lease it to an operator, the responsibility stays with you, unless the lease states otherwise.
gacs.g3p: The rule applies to all non-residential buildings: offices, schools, care institutions, shops, logistics and therefore hotels too. With an event hall, kitchen, pool and climate control per floor, you quickly exceed it.
gacs.g4h: What a BACS must be able to do by law
gacs.g4p: Continuously measure and analyse energy, detect efficiency losses, inform you about improvement options, and communicate with technical systems of different owners, devices and manufacturers.
gacs.g5p: Municipalities and environmental services are the competent authority. They address the owner about the obligation in the first instance.
gacs.g6p: Separate components from different brands are allowed, as long as the functionalities are present together. The practical benchmark is NEN-EN-ISO 52120-1, with function classes from A to D.
gacs.tijdlijn-h2: What is required of you and when
gacs.t1p: BACS required for a heating or air-conditioning system above 290 kW. This requirement already applies now, not at some point in the future.
gacs.t2p: Automatic lighting control becomes mandatory above 290 kW. The control must work per zone and respond to presence and daylight.
gacs.t3p: The BACS obligation will also apply to buildings above 70 kW. This will also affect medium-sized hotels. This European obligation has been enshrined in Dutch law and takes effect on 1 January 2030.
gacs.tijdlijn-noot: The Netherlands implements the European directive in stages. The 290 kW requirement was set as of 1 January 2026. The lighting control requirements and the 70 kW threshold follow in later tranches, with 2030 as the end point. We track which step applies to your site.
gacs.rol-h2: Why separate systems do not make you compliant
gacs.rol-p: Most buildings already have the hardware. What is missing is one layer that reads, connects and steers everything. Without that layer, your installation remains a collection of separate products that do not know each other's data, and that is exactly where the requirements break down. Brands do not have to match, but the systems must be able to talk to each other.
gacs.r1p: Separate meters and controllers produce data, but nobody connects it into a picture of your whole building. Then you cannot see where efficiency is leaking away.
gacs.r2h: Manufacturers that do not understand each other
gacs.r2p: Climate, lighting, energy and charging infrastructure often come from different suppliers. Without an open connection they remain islands.
gacs.r3p: You have to be able to show that you measure, analyse and adjust. Without documented data that is hard to prove to the competent authority.
gacs.ems-label: The role of the Lemnion EMS
gacs.ems-h2: Where the Lemnion EMS fits into a BACS
gacs.ems-p: A BACS is more than a controller that steers the climate. The legal requirements call for continuous measurement, analysis, detecting efficiency losses, informing the manager and being able to work with systems from different manufacturers. Our Energy Management System provides exactly that measurement, analysis and reporting layer. We work brand-independently: your climate installation, energy consumption and charging infrastructure stay in place and start reporting as one system. Where the existing control falls short, we supplement it. That way we build up, step by step, a system that passes the assessment without you replacing everything.
gacs.e1p: All your installations are read and logged continuously at second-level resolution, with trends and consumption history per source.
gacs.e2p: Deviations and efficiency losses are flagged automatically with the cause included, not just as an alarm.
gacs.e3p: You get concrete improvement options in the dashboard, so you know where to adjust and what it delivers.
gacs.e4p: We connect via open protocols with equipment from different manufacturers. Our driver layer speaks Modbus, OCPP, RS485 and REST, among others.
gacs.e5p: Documented monitoring, analyses and exportable reports. You may also demonstrate compliance in another way; we provide the substantiation for that.
gacs.e6p: The control strategy is written specifically for your operation. From the breakfast peak to room hire: your system moves with your hotel.
gacs.norm-h2: The standard is a guideline, not a straitjacket
gacs.norm-p: In practice the technical implementation follows NEN-EN-ISO 52120-1, with function classes from A to D. That standard has no legal status: an equivalent approach is also allowed, for example an assessment by a BACS adviser. If the whole system reaches level C and the energy management component reaches level B, the system is assumed to meet the requirements. There is no brand or type requirement. Separate components from different brands are allowed, as long as the functionalities are present together. We set up and substantiate your system accordingly.
gacs.n1p: We map your capacity, installations and the applicable deadline, so you know whether and when it is your turn.
gacs.n2p: Your existing equipment is integrated into one monitored system. Replacement is usually not necessary.
gacs.n3p: Documented monitoring, analysis and reporting, ready to show.
gacs.ctah: Do you know whether the BACS obligation applies to your hotel?
gacs.ctap: In a short conversation we determine your capacity, which deadline applies and what is needed to be compliant. No obligation.
gacs.label: Further reading
gacs.rl2: All energy challenges at a glance
gacs.t4p: Additional and more sharply defined requirements for the BACS, including that the BACS must be able to monitor indoor air quality (Article 3.146 Bbl). These already apply to the same buildings above 290 kW.
gacs.ems-p2: Please note: the term EMS alone is no guarantee. A simple system that only displays data is usually not enough for the BACS requirements, and neither is a separate controller without analysis. It is about the combination of control, measurement, analysis and open connections. We first assess what your building already has and what is still missing.
gacs.baat-h2: Compliance is not just a cost
gacs.baat-p: A well set-up BACS pays for itself. The system adjusts your consumption, makes losses visible and supplies the data for your reporting. Two concrete benefits come on top of that:
gacs.b1p: If you have a BACS that meets the requirements, your heating and air-conditioning installations no longer need to be inspected separately. That removes a recurring cost.
gacs.b2p: Investments in control technology and efficiency systems can fall under the Energy Investment Allowance: you deduct 40% of the investment from your taxable profit, on top of normal depreciation. There is no separate BACS subsidy; the EIA is the route. We point you to the codes that fit your situation.
gacs.b3p: Better control and insight into your consumption reduce the energy bill. The exact saving differs per building and installation; we calculate it for your situation.
gacs.baat-noot: The tax rules and the exact application per investment vary. No rights can be derived from this information; discuss the EIA application with your accountant.
